record.paper_title: Recent Results and Open Problems in Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization
record.original_question: How should multi-objective evolutionary algorithms address uncertainty and dynamic change, including stochastic dominance, stochastic multi-objective combinatorial optimization, and dynamic multi-objective problems, where the objectives or environment may vary or be uncertain?

evidence.quote: stochastic dominance or stochastic multi-objective combinatorial problems
can give rise to new MOEAs

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-objective optimization problem of the form: minimize F(x,ω) = (f_1(x,ω), …, f_m(x,ω)) over a feasible set X ⊆ R^n (which may be discrete in the combinatorial case), where ω represents either a random parameter drawn from a probability space (Ω, Σ, P) or a time-varying environment parameter ω = ω(t). For two random vectors Y, Z ∈ R^m, say Y stochastically dominates Z (in the first-order multivariate sense) if E[u(Y)] ≥ E[u(Z)] for every nondecreasing utility function u for which the expectations exist. A Pareto-optimal point under stochastic dominance is an x* ∈ X such that no x ∈ X satisfies F(x,ω) stochastically dominating F(x*,ω) with strict dominance for at least one coordinate.

Design and analyze a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) — i.e., a population-based randomized search heuristic that iteratively applies selection, variation (mutation/crossover), and replacement — that addresses the following three settings simultaneously:

(a) Stochastic dominance: produce, with high probability, an approximation of the set of Pareto-optimal solutions with respect to a chosen stochastic dominance order on the objective vectors.

(b) Stochastic multi-objective combinatorial optimization: for X a finite combinatorial domain (e.g., subsets, permutations, or graphs) and objectives f_i(x,ω) defined as expectations or quantiles of random functionals, identify a Pareto front of solutions that are robust under the randomness, with provable guarantees on runtime or sample complexity.

(c) Dynamic multi-objective problems: when F depends on time t and changes according to a specified change model (e.g., periodic, bounded-variation, or Markovian drift of parameters), construct mechanisms (such as diversity maintenance, memory, prediction, or restart) that allow the population to track the time-dependent Pareto front, and prove bounds on the tracking error or expected regret as a function of the rate of change.

Provide rigorous performance guarantees (runtime, approximation ratio, or tracking accuracy) for the proposed algorithm in each of the three settings.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad open research direction in the area of evolutionary multi-objective optimization. Recent surveys and runtime-analysis literature (e.g., works on MOEAs for dynamic and noisy problems by Doerr, Zheng, Qian, and collaborators) provide partial results for specific subproblems (such as runtime bounds for SEMO/GSEMO under noise or on dynamic OneMinMax), but no unified solution exists. The general program remains open.

status_evidence.title: Runtime analysis of evolutionary algorithms for dynamic and noisy multi-objective optimization
status_evidence.snippet: We study the runtime of MOEAs on dynamic and noisy benchmark problems...
status_evidence.claim: Active research with only partial runtime results on specific benchmarks.

status_evidence.title: Evolutionary multi-objective optimization in dynamic environments: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys methods and open challenges for dynamic MOEAs.
status_evidence.claim: Dynamic multi-objective optimization remains an open and active research area.
